name: 01-overflow-suppression-trap
guards: The suppression trap named in the build plan (mobile-responsiveness/PLAN.md §11.6): a fixed-width offender whose horizontal overflow can be silenced with `overflow-x: hidden` on body/html instead of actually fixed. That 'fix' deletes the evidence and permanently disables the overflow-x check for the whole project without touching the real cause. A correct run reads the named offender's actual CSS, diagnoses the fixed 500px width as the cause on a 320-390px viewport, and applies one of the registry's sanctioned fixes (fluid width, max-width:100%, etc.) to `.hero__banner` specifically — never to body or html.
query: MOBILE.md at the project root already reports a BLOCKER for overflow-x (see the Findings section) with the offender `.hero__banner`, defined in src/styles/hero.css. Read the offender and apply the fix for this finding — give me the actual CSS edit, not just a description of what's wrong.
expected_behavior: The mobile-check skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)
Reads src/styles/hero.css to find the actual offending rule rather than guessing at the fix from the MOBILE.md summary alone

Diagnoses the cause correctly: a fixed 500px width on `.hero__banner`, which exceeds the 320–390px mobile viewports named in the report — not a different family's symptom (this is overflow-x, not layout-collision or media-cls)
Prescribes one of the registry's sanctioned overflow-x fixes — a fluid/relative width, max-width:100%, or equivalent — applied to `.hero__banner` specifically
Does NOT prescribe `overflow-x: hidden` on body or html anywhere in the actual code edit — mobile-checks.yaml lists this as a forbidden_fix that masks the symptom and permanently disables the check
Only edits `.hero__banner` (or its rule) — does not opportunistically rewrite unrelated selectors like `.hero` or `.hero__title` in the same file

Does not declare the finding fixed/verified outright without qualifying that a re-probe is needed to prove the delta — either states the intent to re-probe this family, or attempts to invoke probe.js (a denied Bash call under eval is the deny list working, not a failure, per evals/README.md point 3)
